chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Abī Ḥammād, and a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad and others, through different chains, concerning:

The argumentation of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام against ʿĀṣim ibn Ziyād when he wore the cloak and abandoned the proper garment, and his brother al-Rabīʿ ibn Ziyād complained about him to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, saying that by this he had distressed his family and saddened his children.

So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “Bring ʿĀṣim ibn Ziyād to me.” So he was brought to him, and when he saw him, he frowned at him and said to him: “Are you not ashamed before your family? Have you not shown mercy to your children? Do you think that Allah has made the good things lawful for you, yet He dislikes that you take from them? You are too insignificant before Allah for that.”
And does Allah not say: “And the earth, He laid it out for the creatures; therein are fruits and date-palms with sheaths”?
And does Allah not say: “He has let loose the two seas meeting together; between them is a barrier they do not transgress” up to His saying: “From them emerge pearl and coral”?

So by Allah, making use of the blessings of Allah through action is more beloved to Him than speaking of them merely with words. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: “And as for the blessing of your Lord, then proclaim it.”

Then ʿĀṣim said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, then why have you confined yourself in your food to roughness and in your clothing to coarseness?” He said: “Woe to you! Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has obligated the Imams of justice to measure themselves by the weaker people, so that the poor man may not be driven to anguish by his poverty.” So ʿĀṣim ibn Ziyād cast off the cloak and wore the proper garment.

key_terms.أَئِمَّةِ الْعَدْلِ: the Imams of justice who lead with equity and moral responsibility
key_terms.الطَّيِّبَاتِ: the wholesome and lawful good things Allah has permitted
key_terms.الْعَبَاءَ: a cloak associated here with excessive renunciation
key_terms.الْمُلَاءَ: a proper garment or normal clothing
key_terms.ضَعَفَةِ النَّاسِ: the weak and socially vulnerable people
key_terms.نِعَمِ اللَّهِ: the blessings and favors granted by Allah

ai.seo_question: Why did Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام criticize excessive asceticism while himself living simply?
ai.summary: This report teaches that Islam does not praise self-imposed deprivation when it harms one’s family and neglects lawful blessings Allah has permitted. At the same time, it explains that the Imams عليهم السلام, as leaders of justice, may personally adopt a more austere lifestyle in solidarity with the poor and as a duty of leadership.
